comparator.name: Theologie
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official 2026-2027 OER, established on 9 July 2026 and effective from 1 September 2026, defines a three-year, 180-EC Dutch bachelor in Utrecht. Year 1 is a fixed 60-EC theological foundation. Year 2 combines one 24-EC disciplinary track, Greek (15 EC), Hebrew (15 EC) and 6 EC of personal development and worldview; the OER also permits a no-language replacement pathway, but that is an alternative rather than the primary formal table used here. Year 3 consists of a 30-EC minor, 9 EC in exegesis and source languages, a 6-EC theology/media/current-affairs component and a 15-EC final project. The generic registry target names no track. All four tracks carry the same formal weight, so Systematische Theologie, the first track in the OER's official list, is selected by a neutral source-order tie-break fixed independently of UCR fit. The current target and official sources specify the Utrecht programme; registry interest evidence still points to an older Groningen partnership page, so those stale Groningen-specific interests do not override the authoritative Utrecht curriculum.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Utrecht bachelor Theologie and names no disciplinary track. The 2026-2027 OER requires 24 EC in one of four tracks—Systematische Theologie, Historische Theologie, Praktische Theologie or Bijbelwetenschappen—and gives them equal formal weight. No source identifies a default or broader track. The neutral official-order tie-break therefore selects Systematische Theologie, the first listed track, before UCR fit is considered. The main Greek-and-Hebrew pathway in the formal curriculum table is retained; the OER's no-language option is an explicit replacement route rather than the selected primary pathway.

exception.reason: The programme's defining academic identity is sustained Protestant Christian theology and theology-specific method: systematic, historical, practical and biblical theology; Greek and Hebrew; exegesis in the source languages; theology, aesthetics and culture; Reformation history; Judaism and Islam in theological context; personal worldview formation; and a 15-EC final theological project. Only the 30-EC minor is broadly open. UCR offers adjacent philosophy, ethics, history, sociology, politics, literature, art history and cultural analysis, but no sustained theology, scripture, source-language, exegesis or pastoral curriculum. A 24-course UCR schedule assembled from neighbouring humanities and social sciences would erase the target's defining theological sequence and would not be a defensible substantive match.
exception.curriculumContext: The current 2026-2027 OER accounts for exactly 180 EC: a fixed 60-EC first-year foundation; a 60-EC second year built from a 24-EC theology track, 30 EC of Greek and Hebrew and 6 EC of personal development/worldview; and a third year with a 30-EC minor, 15 EC of exegesis and theology-in-public-context study, and a 15-EC final project. The selected Systematische Theologie track is a neutral route instantiation, while the core theological identity, biblical languages and exegesis remain present across available routes. The registry's mapped interest rows cite a Groningen partnership page, but the normalized target, current programme page and governing OER all identify the Utrecht bachelor; the exception is therefore based on the current authoritative Utrecht curriculum rather than stale Groningen-specific evidence.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook course rows, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. GOSPHIL111, GOSPHIL212, GOSPHIL214, GOSPHIL311 and GOSPHIL313 support philosophy, ethics, mind, emotion, agency and the self; GOSHIST111, GOSHIST211 and GOSHIST312 support historical inquiry; GOSSOCI111, GOSSOCI214 and GOSSOCI311 support social analysis; MCCLITR112 and MCCLITR211 engage literary and mythic traditions; MCCHEAM111 and MCCHEAM212 support art-historical and cultural interpretation. None is a dedicated course in Protestant or systematic theology, biblical Greek or Hebrew, scriptural exegesis, historical or practical theology, pastoral formation, Reformation theology or theological research. These adjacent courses cannot sustain a defensible 24-course Theology progression.
